molecules: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH), its kinase and phosphatase
comment: The first experimental test of zero-order ultrasensitivity. Hill coefficient about 2 at IDH concentrations above the Km values.
Proposed: the response of Yan is ultrasensitive and zero-order ultrasensitivity fits the insensitivity of patterning to Yan overexpression.

section: Ultrasensitivity in the response of Cdc25C to Cdk1
comment: Hill coefficient about 4.5 in vitro, about 0.9 with three sites mutated to Glu. Zero-order effects contribute little (dilution studies).

molecules: Cyclin-Cdk1-Cks; Cdc25C (Cks consensus sites T48, T67, T138); Sic1
section: Priming and cooperativity in multisite phosphorylation
comment: Removing the Cks consensus sites makes the Cdc25C response Michaelian. In Sic1 the spacing of the priming site matters.
The paper calls it extra-site ultrasensitivity: any four of eight sites half-maximally release Ste5. Requiring about half of the sites is best.

molecules: Chk1 and Chk2 activate Wee1 and inactivate Cdc25C, both acting on Cdk1
section: Variations on the theme: reciprocal regulation
comment: Names the checkpoint kinases the book leaves out.

molecules: Doxycycline; tetracycline-stimulated activator and tetracycline-inhibited repressor on a Tet-operon reporter
section: Variations on the theme: reciprocal regulation
comment: Hill coefficient 3.2 with both, 1.6 with the activator alone, 1.8 with the repressor alone.
The paper calls it inhibitor ultrasensitivity. p21 about 1 nM, Cdk2 about ten times more abundant.

molecules: C/EBPα reporter with a high-affinity stoichiometric inhibitor (Buchler and Cross)
comment: The inhibitor adds a threshold and high effective Hill coefficients.

molecules: High-affinity decoy transcription factor binding sites (Lee and Maheshri)
comment: Decoys give the transcriptional response a substantial threshold.

molecules: Cyclin B1-Cdk1, Wee1, Sic1 (a high-affinity Cdk1 substrate)
section: Competing Substrates; Ultrasensitivity and time lags
comment: The paper calls it a variation on inhibitor ultrasensitivity: a high-affinity substrate takes up the first kinase. Unlike a plain inhibitor it adds a time lag, and might order the phosphorylation of a master kinase’s targets in time.
Proposed by Sprinzak and co-workers. Such feedback also adds a time lag.

molecules: aTc, tetR, lacI, cI, EYFP reporter
comment: One, two or three intermediaries. Output fold-change exceeds input fold-change when n > 2.

pattern: Interlinked positive and double-negative feedback loops
comment: Bistable over about 4-fold (positive loop alone), 12-fold (double-negative loop alone) and 480-fold (both) ranges of IPTG.

molecules: Three transcriptional repressors in a ring (none named)
comment: A ring of three negative links in place of Goodwin’s three tiers. In the paper’s model it oscillates only when n > 2.

pattern: Relaxation oscillator: negative feedback plus bistable trigger
example: Embryonic cell cycle, the negative loop
comment: The APC/C-Cdc20 response is extremely ultrasensitive (n = 17 to 464). Period about 25 min.

molecules: A receptor oligonucleotide with two overlapping sites for two ligand oligonucleotides
comment: The threshold measured: the first site acts as a stoichiometric buffer. The same system shows a response that rises and then falls as the receptor concentration grows (peak at a receptor to ligand ratio of 1:2), likened to the prozone effect and to scaffold overexpression.
